purpose: Fix, before any forward data exists, the only test that can decide whether the v4 and v6 rules are kept. The 2024-01-01..2026-11-01 backcheck window is spent and contaminated (10 v4 trades, 168 v6 sub-signal trades): it is descriptive only and is not evidence for this test.
decision_context: No new rule versions are built on pre-2026-11-17 history. v3 failed and stays dropped. This file adds no rule, parameter or cost; it pins the existing specs and states what happens after the verdict.

v4.summary: BTCUSDT long/flat; long when close > SMA(2400h) * 1.02, flat when close < SMA(2400h) * 0.98, else unchanged

v6.summary: BTCUSDT + ETHUSDT 50/50 sleeves, no rebalancing; per-coin exposure = mean of the 2% band states for SMA 480/1200/2400/4800h

rules_under_test.unchanged: Rules, lengths, band, clock, costs, segment bounds and criteria are exactly as in the two specs. The runners refuse a spec whose sha256 differs. Any change, including a bug fix that changes results, is a new spec version, and its forward window starts on the day it is committed.

window_utc.embargo: No entry before 2026-11-18T00:00:00Z (the first 24 hours). Each rule starts flat (exposure 0).
window_utc.end_handling: Any open exposure is closed at the open of the 2027-11-17T00:00Z bar with exit cost.
window_utc.warmup: Signals may use closes before the start (past data only, causal). v4 needs 2400 hourly bars and v6 needs 4800 before the start.

data.source: Binance public spot 1h klines (data.binance.vision), monthly and daily zips, each verified against its .CHECKSUM before use, as defined in each spec.
data.causal_only: The state after the close of bar i is held from the open of bar i+1 to the open of bar i+2.
data.gaps: Missing hours are counted and reported. A gap longer than 24 hours inside the window is an error, not something to repair by hand.
data.where: Research machine only. Not on the VPS. No exchange API keys: public files only.

costs.v4: equity * (1 - 0.0012) on every entry and exit
costs.v6: sleeve equity * (1 - 0.0012 * |change in exposure|) on every exposure change

benchmark.info_only: Buy-and-hold (BTC for v4, 50/50 BTC+ETH for v6) and the v4 rule on 50/50 BTC+ETH are reported for information. They play no part in pass/fail, because holding BTC is not an option.

failure_criteria.applies_to: each rule on its own; v4 and v6 are judged separately
fail_if_any: total net return after costs over the full window <= 0 (does not beat cash)
max drawdown of the equity curve >= 0.35 (v6: portfolio equity curve)
failure_criteria.boundary_note: The committed runners pass only when max drawdown < 0.35, so a drawdown of exactly 35% counts as a failure. This is the stricter reading of 'above 35%' and matches the code.
failure_criteria.consequence_of_fail: The rule is dropped. No re-tuning, no re-run, no new window for the same rule family on the same idea.
failure_criteria.consequence_of_pass: The rule survives one out-of-sample year. Trade counts are far below a few hundred, so a pass is weak evidence and is not a profitability claim. A pass is not approval for live trading; Phase 3/4 gates and trading-safety still apply.

evaluation.verdict_runs: Once per rule, on the complete window: the first run on data that includes the 2027-11-17T00:00Z bar for every symbol (that day's daily zip is published around 2027-11-18). The verdict from that run stands; it is not re-run, re-ordered or replaced.
evaluation.verdict_enforcement: The current runners compute a verdict only when the window is complete but do not block a second complete run. Until a marker check is added, the operator runs the complete-window verdict once and commits the JSON output with its git_commit and spec_sha256.
evaluation.interim_reads: Allowed for information only (the runners return verdict 'interim_no_verdict'). They never change the rule, costs, window or criteria. A drawdown above 35% during the window can be reported as an interim fact but the formal verdict waits for the complete run.
report_must_include: window, first and exit bar, missing hours per symbol
spec version, spec sha256, runner version, git commit
total net return after costs, CAGR, Sharpe, max drawdown
trade counts: v4 round trips; v6 sub-signal round trips per coin and portfolio total
average exposure and exposure at the last signal
verdict per rule against failure_criteria, plus the caveat that trade counts are too low to be strong evidence

safety.paper_only: execution_enabled=false stays enforced. This test places no orders, paper or real, and needs nothing on the VPS.

known_limits: v4 makes about 3 round trips a year, so the window will hold only a handful of trades.
v6 sub-signal round trips overcount independent decisions; BTC and ETH are highly correlated, so v4 and v6 are not independent tests.
One year is one market regime. A sideways year can fail both rules without saying much about other regimes, and a bull year can pass them without proving an edge.
